title: SYSK Selects: Is there treasure on Oak Island?
summary: A rerun Selects episode of Stuff You Should Know on the Oak Island Mystery off Nova Scotia. The hosts cover the legend of the Money Pit, which began when teenager Daniel McGinnis found a pulley block on an oak tree in 1795 and dug a depression that later flooded. They describe the subsequent expeditions (the Onslow Company, the Truro company, the Eldorado Company, Frederick Blair's Oak Island Treasure Company, Robert Dunfield's 1960s-era digging, and the Triton Alliance with Dan Blanketship and David Tobias, who reported an underwater camera sighting in 1970), the coconut fiber and charcoal finds, the man-made five-finger drainage system, and theories about pirates, the Knights Templar, the Freemasons, Marie Antoinette's jewels, and Francis Bacon. They note the scarcity of hard evidence, the skeptic versus believer divide, and the later History Channel show. The episode closes with a listener mail story about poison ivy in burning firewood.

segments.title: Rerun intro and Oak Island setup
segments.summary: Josh introduces this Selects rerun of the Oak Island episode from 2015. The hosts note how divisive the island is and how the 'curse' is largely a TV creation. They joke about circus performers Mildred and Robert Restall.

segments.title: Daniel McGinnis and the first digging
segments.summary: A sixteen-year-old Daniel McGinnis finds a pulley block on an oak tree and a cleared depression, and starts digging with friends. They find oak platforms every ten feet, creating the Money Pit, and give up after a few days without the tools and funding to continue.

segments.title: Onslow Company expedition and coconut fiber
segments.summary: Nine years later the Onslow Company funds a return dig. They find coconut fiber, charcoal and putty, and a reported cipher stone at about ninety feet, with no surviving evidence of its inscription. The pit floods with water overnight, and the expedition gives up.

segments.title: Truro company and the five-finger drain
segments.summary: The Truro company in 1849 suspects the flooding is deliberate and searches the shoreline. They find a man-made drainage system, the five-finger drain, lined with coconut fiber, which funnels tidewater toward the money pit. Believers see a booby trap, while skeptics see natural causes.

segments.title: Legends: Knights Templar, Freemasons, Marie Antoinette, Francis Bacon
segments.summary: The hosts go through the proposed owners of the buried treasure: the Knights Templar and the Holy Grail or Ark of the Covenant, Freemasons, Marie Antoinette's jewels, and Francis Bacon's manuscripts and mercury flasks.

segments.title: Eldorado Company, Blair parchment, and Dunfield
segments.summary: Treasure fever after the California Gold Rush brings the Eldorado Company in 1866, whose efforts to block water destroy landmarks. Frederick Blair in the 1890s finds a small piece of parchment with letters. In the twentieth century, Robert Dunfield builds a causeway, digs to about 140 feet, and finds porcelain but no major riches.

segments.title: Triton Alliance, Blanketship, and the curse
segments.summary: The Triton Alliance (Tobias and Blanketship) uses an underwater camera in 1970 and reports seeing evidence of human remains and treasure chests. Dan Blanketship remains on the island. The hosts mention a dispute with Fred Nolan, Nolan's Cross, and the History Channel show about the Lagina brothers. They conclude that the physical evidence is thin.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: A brief break between the content and the listener mail.

segments.title: Poison ivy follow-up from JB
segments.summary: Listener JB describes how burning poison ivy logs as a child sent her sister to the emergency room with a swollen face, because the sap was in the smoke. The hosts laugh about the passport photo.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: The hosts thank JB and invite listeners to send stories and visit the website.
